answer_plain: Where the soil community has no genes for eating carbon monoxide, the twin gives exactly zero carbon-monoxide uptake. Where the genes are present it gives a small uptake, about 144 millionths of a mole per m² over two weeks (21 to 501).
answer_science: In samples whose reasoner-entailed CO-carrier share is zero (51PRr3, 55PRr1, 55PRr3, 55Sr1, 58PRr3), CO uptake is zero by deduction: the community factor γ_CO is zero, so uptake is zero for every parameter draw and the interval is [0, 0]. In samples with carriers (10Dr2, V53PRr2), 14-day CO uptake has a median of 126 µmol m⁻² (90 % interval 21.1 to 501 µmol m⁻²), with the CO rate constant k_CO explaining most of the variance (S_T = 0.84).
baseline_label: One 12 mm rain on day 1 in the selected sample community

limits_plain: The range shows how much the answer moves when uncertain numbers in the models are varied; the models themselves could also be wrong. A missing gene in recovered DNA means the twin sets that pathway to zero, though very rare unsequenced microbes could still exist in the sand.
limits_science: Absence of entailment reflects the genomic evidence in the sample; a carrier below the detection limit of the metagenome would change the deduction. The open-sample uptake uses the reference community factor.

admissibility.scope: Joint parameter and literature-constant uncertainty only; excludes model-structure error.
